newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour windfall tax aimed at 30 utilities - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour windfall tax aimed at 30 utilities - paper.

text.p: The UK's opposition Labour party plans to raise more than five billion stg from a windfall tax on the profits of up to 30 privatised utilities, the Daily Telegraph newspaper reported in its Friday edition.

"We think five billion stg is the conservative end of the spectrum," the newspaper quoted a spokesman for the shadow chancellor Gordon Brown. "In principle all privatised utilities will be considered. We would not want to discriminate unfairly."
The Daily Telegraph added that a leaked city report indicated that most companies could comfortably afford a levy of more than five billion stg.
On Thursday, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke urged a parliamentary committee to demand that Labour make clear which privatised utilities would have to pay its windfall tax.
